newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades steady against rising outrights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades steady against rising outrights.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices remained firm on an outright basis Monday afternoon, while prices for grade differentials took a steady ride.

Cash traders reported a subdued trading session, with only a nominal number of trades for the grades. Outright cash prices have gained in-line with a surging futures market, supported by press reports linking an Iranian government official with suspected bombers of the American barracks in Saudi Arabia last year.
Iran was already under pressure following a German court ruling linking Tehran with political assassinations in 1992.

The court said the Iranian government was involved with the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, prompting most European Union governments to recall ambassadors from Tehran to express disapproval.

Traders said tensions from the possible link to the U.S. bombing could provoke military or economic reprisals against the Islamic republic. However, no immediate threat was seen to Iran's oil industry, which pumps around 3.7 million barrels per day of oil, the second largest amount within OPEC.

For the U.S. cash market, traders said the latest deals for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James were done at a 29 cts and 28 cts discount to the benchmark May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, nearly steady from morning trades at 30 cts under level.
May WTI was currently charting gains of some 45 cts to $19.95-20.05 a barrel, steady with the June month.
Other deals saw Midland/WTI sell at 29 cts under the marker, and May Postings Plus at $1.75, 5 cts stronger than late on Friday.
Traders said Brent offerings in the Gulf were being discussed, but dealings were quiet ahead of the expected announcement Tuesday for the May program.
IPE May Brent futures also expire on Tuesday.
